newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Cyclone Drena downgraded to depression as hits NZ.
newsitem.headline: Cyclone Drena downgraded to depression as hits NZ.

text.p: Northern New Zealand prepared for severe winds on Friday as the remains of Cyclone Drena bore down on the country, but forecasters said rainfall may not be as high as first thought.
The Meteorological Service has downgraded Drena to a deep depression but says strong wind warnings remain in force.

On Thursday MetService predicted hurricane force winds gusting up to 130 km/hour (80 miles/hour) at times in exposed areas of the north -- strong enough to force cars off the road, uproot trees and flip camper vans.

Chief forecaster Augie Auer told Radio New Zealand a shift in the centre of the storm, which is 350 km northwest of the North Island and moving south, meant it would bring solid rain but not as much as predicted.
"Satellite images and radar show that Drena is maintaining strong winds but rainfall over the area may be less than originally forecast," Auer said.
The Coromandel region, which bore the brunt of Fergus, could still be in line for 250 millimetres of rain over the next 24 hours, down from a forecast 350 mm, Auer warned.
Northland, which is currently getting steady rain, can expect around 50 mm, down from previous forecasts of 250 mm.
Drena is the country's second tropical storm in less than two weeks, at the height of the summer holiday season.
The upper North Island took a battering late in December from the remnants of tropical cyclone Fergus, which was also downgraded to a deep depression as it hit New Zealand.
Auer warned against complacency in the face of Drena simply because Fergus did not live up to expectations.
He emphasised Drena was still packing a punch, with winds averaging 100 km/hour at the tip of the North Island and the possibility of damaging gusts in Auckland mid-afternoon.

Auckland police are warning of the combined impact of Drena and spring high tides, and say if winds rise as expected, motorcyclists, caravans and trailers should not use the motorway bridge over Auckland Harbour.
Auckland city Civil Defence is recommending people secure items such as outdoor furniture, and tape over large windows.
